County websites with sitemap problems

1,082 of 2,400 fully scanned U.S. county government websites have a sitemap problem. A map, the share in each state, and every site listed, from ScanGov homepage scans.

  • Sites: 2815
  • Last scan: 10/3/2026

Of the 2,400 fully scanned U.S. county sites we tested, 1,082 (45%) have a sitemap problem. Among states with at least 10 tested sites, Texas has the highest share at 79% and New Jersey the lowest at 17%. A sitemap is an XML file that lists the pages on a site. Search engines and AI agents read it to find pages they would otherwise miss, and robots.txt is where they look for its address. A site counts as failing when it fails any of the checks behind this page: Sitemap status, Sitemap XML, and Sitemap in robots.txt.

About these checks

A sitemap is an XML file that lists the pages on a site. Search engines and AI agents read it to find pages they would otherwise miss, and robots.txt is where they look for its address. The botability checks behind this page test each part of that. A site with a working sitemap and no robots.txt file counts as passing here, since there is no file to list the sitemap in.

  • Sitemap status. The sitemap file loads and returns a successful response. Search engines cannot find all your pages.
  • Sitemap XML. The sitemap file uses the required XML format. Search engines cannot read your sitemap.
  • Sitemap in robots.txt. The robots.txt file links to the sitemap. Search engines take longer to find your pages.

Guidance

  • Sitemap status standard, with how to fix it
  • Sitemap XML standard, with how to fix it
  • Sitemap in robots.txt standard, with how to fix it
  • sitemaps.org
  • Google Search Central
  • Counties botability rankings

About this data

ScanGov scans the homepage of each county government site on our county list. Scores come from the checks listed on standards.scangov.org. Sites were scanned between 7/18/2026 and 10/2/2026; each site's report shows its own scan date. A site counts as fully scanned when its homepage returned successfully and sent the scanner its page content. Averages, grade shares, failure rates, and ranks use fully scanned sites only. We weren't able to fully scan 396 sites because they did not respond, blocked the scanner, or returned no page content. They appear in the table without grades, each with its scan status, and are left out of every figure. Grades follow the ScanGov grade scale, and rank follows the ScanGov ranking method. The full dataset, including every county's raw results, is published in the ScanGov data repository.

19 fully scanned county sites have no result for these checks and are left out of the share.
